fit_to_spice.description: Make a passive SPICE subcircuit from a Touchstone file (S-parameters of a passive N-port, for example from an EM simulation), with a typed error report. Method: vector fitting with common poles, a Hamiltonian passivity test, residue perturbation when the test fails, and a subcircuit of C, G, F and V elements that ngspice and Xyce both read (pins p1 p1_ref p2 p2_ref ...). The subcircuit is noiseless: each conductance is a G source controlled by its own voltage, because a resistor of the realisation adds noise that has no relation to the passive. A noise analysis therefore leaves out the thermal noise of the loss of the passive (the noise figure is optimistic by up to the loss of a passive at the input). Inputs: touchstone (the file, relative to the design root; version 1 or 2, S-parameters only), uses (required: the frequencies at which the simulation will use the model, {"band_hz": [f_lo, f_hi]} or {"f0_hz": f0, "harmonics": H} for harmonic balance, and "dc" (default true: the simulation solves a DC point through the model, as every SPICE analysis does)), dc_policy (optional, "model": accept the DC value of the model when the data has no 0 Hz point; the response reports it), fit_band_hz (optional [f_lo, f_hi]: fit only the data in this band), order (optional, the number of poles; default: the lowest even order from 2 to max_order, default 40, that meets limits.max_abs_ds), limits (optional: max_abs_ds, default 0.01; l_rel_error and q_rel_error with lq_band_hz), lq_band_hz (optional [f_lo, f_hi], 1-port or 2-port: the error of the series L and Q in this band; a |dS| limit alone can pass a model with a large Q error), name (the subcircuit name; default the file stem), verify (default ["ngspice", "xyce"]: simulate the subcircuit in each simulator with AC runs and compare with the model and, on a uniform data grid, with the data). The run is refused (status failed, every measurement failed, no subcircuit) when uses is missing, when the data band does not cover every frequency in uses (an extrapolation is not supported by the data), when uses.dc is true and the data has no 0 Hz point without dc_policy "model", when the fit does not meet the limits, or when the model is not passive after enforcement. Measurements: order, fit_max_abs_ds, fit_rms_abs_ds, s<i><j>_max_abs_ds and s<i><j>_rms_abs_ds per entry, l_max_rel_error and q_max_rel_error (with lq_band_hz), passivity_margin (1 - the largest singular value of the model, sampled from 0 Hz to 10^4 times the band end and at the poles; the Hamiltonian test has no crossing), enforcement_max_abs_ds (the change of the model at the data points by the enforcement), band_min_hz, band_max_hz, verify_<sim>_max_abs_ds (simulated subcircuit against the data) and verify_<sim>_model_max_abs_ds (against the rational model; above 1e-4 is an error). Outputs: work/<name>.lib (role subckt), work/<name>.model.s<N>p (role touchstone: the model at the data frequencies), work/fit.json (role report: poles, errors, passivity, DC values of the model, re-simulation), and the decks and logs of the re-simulation. The kernel adds the Touchstone summary (ports, band, passivity, reciprocity) to the input and to the model file.
